judge_guidance: PASS only if the note (a) states the video is digitally manipulated / deepfaked — NOT authentic footage of Macron or Zelensky dancing — with Macron's face superimposed onto unrelated archival dancers, AND (b) is clearly worded and easy to parse. It must AVOID the original note's failure of being hard to understand: do NOT bury the point in a confusing clause like 'most originating from his pre-presidency comedy sketches'. It is fine to briefly note Zelensky was a pre-presidency entertainer, but the core message — the footage is fake/manipulated — must be unambiguous. Cite a reputable fact-check. FAIL if the note treats the dancing footage as real, or is so convoluted a reader cannot tell what is being corrected.
